3.0.s.en: (1) The beginning of the Baptist's ministry

3.0.0.en: St. Luke specifies the time of the beginning of the ministry of John the Baptist by the kings and governors belonging to the Roman Empire, and it is also the time of the beginning of Christ's ministry, because the Baptist preceded Him by six months. Tiberius Caesar: the Roman emperor at that time.

3.0.1.en: Pontius Pilate: who judged Christ, and was the Roman governor over all of Judea.

3.0.2.en: Judea: the southern part of the land of the Jews.

3.0.3.en: Herod: this is Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, the killer of the children of Bethlehem.

3.0.4.en: Tetrarch: the Romans divided the region into four provinces.

3.0.5.en: Galilee: the northern part of the land of the Jews.

3.0.6.en: Philip: son of Herod the Great and husband of Herodias.

3.0.7.en: Judea: this is Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, the killer of the children of Bethlehem.

3.0.8.en: Ituraea, Trachonitis, Abilene: places adjoining Judea and Galilee.

3.0.9.en: As a historian, St. Luke also mentions two rulers over neighboring regions, namely Philip the son of Herod the Great and Lysanias. The date, as the Fathers established, is approximately AD 26, on the basis that the birth of Christ was about 4 BC, and from this his precision as a historian appears.

3.1.0.en: The word of God came unto: that is, the work of the Spirit in John the Baptist to begin his ministry, and to declare the word of God to the crowds and call them to repentance.

3.1.1.en: The wilderness: that is, the desert of Judea.

3.1.2.en: According to the law of the Jews the high priest remained so throughout his life, but the Romans intervened and deposed Annas and brought in Caiaphas, the husband of his daughter, and Annas kept his authority, therefore Luke mentions him.

3.2.0.en: The baptism of repentance: John's baptism was accompanied by people's confession of their sins, so it was a preparation for the sacraments of Baptism and Confession.

3.2.1.en: John was brought up in the wilderness for about thirty years under God's care, then began his ministry in the regions around the Jordan, calling for repentance and return to God, and whoever accepted his word he baptized in the river Jordan to begin a new life with God. This was a preparation for Christ's preaching of repentance and His baptizing with the Holy Spirit, so that men receive the new nature from Christ the Redeemer and their sins are forgiven.

3.2.2.en: It is understood from the verse that John moved about among the regions around the river Jordan, and was not settled in one place.

3.2.3.en: Repentance and the sacrament of Confession are two essential conditions for the forgiveness of your sins, so hasten to your father of confession to be freed from the dominion of sin and begin a life of righteousness. Repeat this with insistence in daily repentance before God and confession every month in the Church, and your life will always be renewed.

3.3.0.en: Thus the prophecy of Isaiah (Isa 40:3-5) is fulfilled about John the Baptist, who goes before and prepares the way of Christ by his preaching in the wilderness and his calling the crowds to repentance and an upright life, just as the kings' messengers used to go before them, calling on the people to remove the obstacles in the road the kings would travel. What is meant here is repentance from the sins that obstruct God's way within people's hearts.

3.4.0.en: All flesh: a prophecy of the acceptance of all the nations into faith and salvation in the name of the Lord Christ (Isa 40:3-5).

3.4.1.en: Isaiah prophesies that the Gentiles, sunk in sin like valleys, will be filled with the Holy Spirit through their faith and their return to God. And as for the Jews, lofty in their pride and in their boasting of their origin and their Law, like mountains and high hills, when they come to repentance and faith in the humble Christ they too will be humbled, and everyone who was crooked or rough (rough ways) in the life of sin will be made straight by accepting the salvation of Christ.

3.5.0.en: When John proclaimed repentance and baptism for the forgiveness of sins, great crowds of Jews went out to him to be baptized by him, for they felt that he was a great prophet.

3.5.1.en: God gave him a strong awe in their hearts, but the Baptist was not preoccupied with their multitude, knowing that they had not repented with all their hearts, and that they had undergone baptism because they were children of the prophets and children of God, so he was compelled to rebuke them that they might truly repent, and described them as a generation of vipers, because the viper crawls on its belly on the ground, so it signifies attachment to earthly things, and it is also poisonous and harms everyone around it. Some kinds of them eat their mother's belly so that she dies and they come forth to life, so it signifies selfish conduct and wronging others, even those who are close. And he warned them of the wrath of God the Judge that was coming upon them if they did not repent.

3.6.0.en: He called them to do good to everyone, for this is the proof of true repentance.

3.6.1.en: And he surprised them by saying that they should not rely on the honor of their sonship to Abraham, for this would not stop God's wrath against them, and even more than this, he declared to them that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. What is meant by the stones is the stony hearts in the children of the Gentiles, because of the hardness of their hearts like stone; He is able to make them hearts of flesh that believe in Him and love Him. Thus the Jews perish because of the hardness of their hearts and their lack of repentance, and the Gentiles are saved by their faith in Christ and their walking in righteousness.

3.6.2.en: Do not rely, my brother, on the fact that your name is Christian, for this will not protect you from God's wrath; rather you must offer tears of repentance and regret your sins every day, and leave your evil works and do good to everyone and become a true son of Christ, who loved all and gave Himself for them.

3.7.0.en: The Baptist grew more severe, and declared that the hour was near, for Christ would begin His preaching shortly; and if they did not repent and believe in Him, the axe, that is, the word of God, which is like a two-edged sword, would judge everyone who does not believe in Him. By the root of the trees are meant the leaders, priests and teachers, whom the word of Christ condemns before the rest of the Jews because of their lack of repentance, and nothing awaits them but the eternal fire.

3.7.1.en: Remembering death and judgment is necessary for our lives, so that we may awaken from our laziness and pride and our delight in the evil lusts of the world and our persistence in the sin that we have justified so as not to repent.

3.8.s.en: (3) The Baptist's answers to the questions

3.8.0.en: The Baptist's words affected the hearts of his hearers, so they inquired about the practical application of his words, and the crowds of poor Jews asked him about the meaning of repentance and its fruit, and he spoke to them about love and giving. He that hath two coats (that is, a poor man who owns only two garments) let him give one to him that hath none. The coat is what is worn inside beneath the outer clothes, that is, the least a person needs. Likewise whoever has food, even a little, let him give part of it to the hungry. Thus we find ourselves moving in John's words from the Old Testament to the New, preparing for the self-giving love of Christ and the life of fellowship in the Church, and that giving is required not only of the rich but also of the poor.

3.9.0.en: The tax collectors: they were a group of Jewish farmers, but richer than ordinary people, who undertook to pay the Roman taxes for a specified Jewish district and then collected them from individuals with the help of Roman soldiers, and whoever paid more to the Roman state was chosen to collect the taxes. They would add to the required taxes and so became rich, but they were an example of love of money and exploitation of the weak, however needy they were. John did not ask them to leave their jobs, but declared to them the importance of justice and leaving the love of money, that is, to collect only what they had paid or a little more by which to support themselves.

3.10.0.en: Among those who went out to the Baptist were some soldiers, who, since they had authority over everyone, exploited it in wronging others and extorting their money, and whoever did not obey them they would fabricate charges against and complain of to the Roman authority, so they too fell into exploiting their work to collect money. So John asked them to be content with their wages (their rations).

3.10.1.en: Do you feel for those around you and hasten to help them, even if you have little money or effort? Do you exploit your work, position and connections for your own benefit, or for the love of others and helping them? Remember that Christ used His position as God to give you His full love on the Cross, and what have you given Him?

3.11.0.en: More than 400 years had passed during which no prophet had appeared in Israel, and they believed that the coming prophet would be the Messiah. Therefore, when John appeared calling to them like the prophets to repent so as to be saved from divine punishment, in addition to his asceticism regarding material things and his boldness in speech, they thought that he was the Christ.

3.12.0.en: The humility of the Baptist appears, for he declares himself a servant preparing the way for Christ, and his baptism with water is a symbol of the cleansing from sin that would be accomplished in the baptism of Christ with the Holy Spirit, and this is joined with fire because the Holy Spirit burns up sin like fire. Here is a prophetic declaration about the Holy Spirit, who would work on the day of Pentecost through the hands of the disciples and then their successors the bishops and priests in baptizing the believers, and he declares his unworthiness to stoop down and unloose the latchet of Christ's shoes, for this is an honor greater than he can receive.

3.12.1.en: St. Cyril the Great proves the divinity of Christ from this verse, because Christ here gives the Holy Spirit, that is, His own Spirit, so He is God; and only one who has a body can wear shoes, so He is the incarnate Christ and the God who became man, and this is also a proof of His Incarnation.

3.12.2.en: St. Gregory the Great says that the shoe signifies the humanity of Christ, so John declares that he is not able to unloose its latchet, that is, to uncover the mysteries of the divine Incarnation; how wonderful is God's condescension to become incarnate for our sake!

3.12.3.en: Do not attribute the glory to yourself, my brother, but to God with thanksgiving, especially when people praise you.

3.13.0.en: John speaks about Christ the Judge, and compares the day of judgment to the day of winnowing wheat, that is, separating its grains from the husk surrounding them, which is called chaff, in a wide place called the threshing floor. The fan, that is, the winnowing fork, is a wooden staff with several prongs at its end like a fork, which lifts the grains of wheat into the air, and by the action of the air or the wind the light husk surrounding the grain flies far away, while the grain falls in its place because it is heavier, and thus the grains are separated from the chaff. Then the wheat, which is the believers filled with the grace of God, is gathered into His garner, that is, the paradise of delight, having been tested by the wind, which signifies trials, and their strength and steadfastness were revealed; but the empty husks in which there are no grains signify the people who are empty of God's grace and faith, and trials expose them as mere chaff to be burned with fire, that is, eternal torment.

3.13.1.en: And the One who holds the fan, that is, the winnowing fork, is Christ the Judge, who rewards His children with bliss, but the wicked He casts into the eternal fire.

3.13.2.en: Do not neglect Christ's call to you to repent; enjoy His holy Mysteries, and remain steadfast in His Church, and you will not be troubled by the winds of trials, and thus you secure your happy eternity.

3.14.0.en: The original aim of John's preaching was calling them to repentance, in preparation for the preaching of Christ and His declaring the greatness of His salvation which He offers to mankind.

3.14.1.en: To this were added many teachings and exhortations, that is, consolations with which John encouraged the souls of his hearers, which the Holy Bible cannot contain to write.

3.15.0.en: The Baptist's ministry did not stop at the common people but extended to all classes, even to King Herod himself, who is called Herod Antipas, who was distinguished by many evils and wickedness, especially in his seizing Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, to be his wife during his brother's lifetime.

3.16.0.en: Herod could not bear John's bold rebukes and wanted to silence this voice, so he shut him up in prison, and afterward killed him; but the voice continued to cry out, rebuking his conscience, so that when the preaching of Christ spread, he said that it was the Baptist whom he had killed who had risen again.

3.16.1.en: Herod imprisoned John after he had baptized Christ, but St. Luke mentions the imprisonment here because it is connected with John's rebuke of him.

3.16.2.en: Added yet this above all: he added to all his evils for which he was notorious that he shut up the great prophet beloved by the people, John the Baptist.

3.16.3.en: Do not reject the voice of God that rebukes you for your sins through the tongue of those around you, for even if you silence them by your anger and authority, your conscience continues to rebuke you, and if you silence it, judgment awaits you .... Now is an opportunity for repentance, so you may recover your peace and purity through your humility.

3.17.0.en: John's baptism showed mankind's need of repentance and salvation, and Christ, the representative of mankind, came to be baptized although He was without sin, but to bear our sins and fulfill all righteousness on our behalf, and to be an example for us in coming to baptism, but the baptism that is with the Holy Spirit in the New Testament; and He prayed to be an example for us in prayer also, so that heaven is opened to us and we have a relationship with God.

3.18.0.en: Here the Holy Trinity appears clearly: the Son in the water, and the Holy Spirit, who has been in the Son from eternity, appearing in bodily form, which is a dove, and the voice of the Father from heaven declaring that the One in the water is the one true Son, in whom is all His pleasure; therefore the Church calls the Feast of Theophany the Feast of the Divine Manifestation.

3.18.1.en: If Christ fulfilled all righteousness on our behalf, may we make up for the shortcomings of others and cover their faults and do what they ought to do for the sake of God and out of love for them, so that we are truly children of God and deserve the heavenly praise and divine blessings.

4.0.0.en: After the baptism of Christ and the appearance of the Holy Spirit upon Him like a dove, this was a sign of the beginning of Christ's ministry, so here He declares His being full of the Holy Spirit and led by Him, although the Holy Spirit is His own Spirit from eternity; but here is a declaration to us to make us know the Holy Trinity and the importance of the Holy Spirit's leading of our lives. If the servant is not first filled with the Spirit, through his attachment to the holy Mysteries, prayer and reading the Holy Bible, and also his humble submission to God's guidance, he cannot serve successfully.

4.1.0.en: Christ fasted forty days before the beginning of His ministry to declare the importance of the goal, which is the spiritual life, accompanied by renunciation of material things.

4.1.1.en: He was tempted throughout the forty days by the devil, and the devil could not prevail over Him, because His asceticism in fasting and His solitude for prayer in the wilderness nullify every power of the devil, as Christ Himself said about Satan, "This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting" (Mk 9:29).

4.1.2.en: Christ fasted only forty days, like Moses and Elijah, so as not to do anything beyond human capacity, and He hungered to confirm His true humanity in which He is like us. Therefore we can imitate His fasting and His prayers with quiet retreat, and so overcome all the devil's wars.

4.2.0.en: There were many temptations throughout the forty-day fast, but at its end the strongest temptations appeared, and they are these three mentioned here.

4.2.1.en: So Satan came to Christ in the wilderness of Judea, after He felt hunger from fasting forty days, and focused his words on Christ's need of food.

4.2.2.en: The devil always chooses the points of need and weakness in us to fight us with them, so that his words may seem reasonable and we accept them and fall into sin.

4.2.3.en: Here he wanted Christ to use His divine power for the benefit of His comfort as a man, and this of course is rejected, because Christ came to be like us in everything, and to bear the hardest sufferings for our sake and to triumph over the devil while in this human weakness, that we too may triumph in Him.

4.2.4.en: If thou be the Son of God: the devil's words are doubting and provoking, as is his habit in his wars against us through the tongues of those around us, and by this question he wanted to understand the truth about Jesus: if He turned the stone into bread he would know that He is the Christ and keep away from Him, and if He said "I cannot," he would know that He is a mere man and fight Him and defeat Him.

4.2.5.en: The Fathers say that the devil offers only stones and not bread, so that our hearts become stony and hard. And they say that what may be meant by the stone is heresies, which become to us a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense instead of the word of God, the true food.

4.3.0.en: In His answer Christ turned attention to a more important matter, which is spiritual nourishment by the word of God. He relied in this on what is written in the Torah (Deut 8:3), to teach us to rest our lives on God's commandments. If a person is satisfied by the word of God and by partaking of the Mysteries, he can bear the sufferings of life and the weakness of the body, and is content with what he has even if it is little.

4.4.0.en: The second temptation is the desire to possess the material things of the world, and in order to dazzle Christ in his temptation, the devil took Him up to a high mountain, so that vast areas of the surrounding countries appeared in all their glory.

4.5.0.en: With audacity and deceit the devil declared his dominion over all the earth and his ability to give it to whomever he wishes, although he rules only over the wicked; but he is a liar from the beginning, and he deceives us to shake our faith if we believe his lies.

4.6.0.en: He asked Christ to worship him, which is the worship of devotion and submission, and then He would give Him to reign over the earth and mankind without enduring the sufferings of the Cross. He always calls us to the easy life and immersion in pleasures and love of possession, so that we give up our vigilance against sin and our spiritual striving, preoccupied with the delights and splendors of the world. This is the worship that he asks of us, and consequently we abandon our prayers and our love for God.

4.7.0.en: The Lord Christ did not discuss with the devil his lies in claiming authority over the earth, to teach us to flee from dialogue with Satan's thoughts. He answered him with what is written in the Holy Bible, which is worshiping God alone (Deut 6:13), and Jesus' word "Get thee behind me," that we may learn to drive away all his thoughts, however pleasant, tempting or convincing they may seem.

4.7.1.en: Where is your heart? ... If it is in the love of God and attachment to Him, you will not be affected by any of the devil's enticements of money, lust or possessions.

4.8.0.en: The third temptation was in Jerusalem, in the Temple, that is, the holiest place. The devil fights in every place, even in the Church. The pinnacle of the Temple is its highest place, and he repeats his doubting and provoking of Christ, so that He would use His power for His personal glory, by throwing Himself down from the highest place with the crowds massed below in the Temple, and then the angels would appear carrying Him, so that He would come down among the crowds and begin His ministry. The devil's words seem convincing, but their reality is drawing Jesus into pride, love of display, and people's glorifying Him.

4.8.1.en: And the sin of pride fights everyone, especially those in office or authority, and it also fights the servants and priests who are in the holy place.

4.9.0.en: When Satan found Jesus relying on what is written, he too relied on what is written, but with deceit and wrong interpretation, for he took part of (Ps 91:11, 12), which applies to God's keeping of His children if any problems and temptations from the devil befall them, as verse 13 makes clear: "Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet," that is, God keeps them by His angels and they triumph over the devil, the old serpent. These verses do not mean a display of our power to obtain honor from people.

4.10.0.en: Jesus answered him with the words of the Holy Bible from (Deut 6:16), which is that it is not right to tempt God to test His truthfulness, but rather we trust in His promises if a temptation meets us.

4.10.1.en: Beware of pursuing honor and love of display, trusting in God's promises and His support for you, and to the extent that you hide yourself, you are raised in God's sight and He rewards you, not only in eternity but with peace and joy in this life.

4.11.0.en: After Christ spent forty days in the wilderness of Judea, He returned to Galilee, where He was brought up in one of its cities, Nazareth. The Evangelist stresses that He was led by the Holy Spirit, to teach us submission to the work of the Spirit in us and not to our own thinking.

4.11.1.en: Christ went to Galilee twice: the first is the one mentioned here after His baptism, then He returned to Judea, and after about a year He visited Galilee after the imprisonment of John the Baptist, as Matthew and Mark mention (Mt 4:12, Mk 1:14), and John mentioned both visits (Jn 1:43, Jn 4:3).

4.11.2.en: This means that He visited Nazareth also twice: the first Luke mentions here and the second Matthew and Mark mention at His visit to Galilee (Mt 13:54-58, Mk 6:1-6).

4.12.0.en: Jesus began to teach in the synagogues of the cities of Galilee, and likewise the villages around Capernaum, the center of His preaching in Galilee, where He taught and performed many miracles, which aroused the jealousy of the people of the city of Nazareth because He had not begun with them. He taught with authority and power, and the hearers were amazed and glorified Him.

4.12.1.en: V. 16 As his custom was: Christ was accustomed to attend the synagogue during His stay in Nazareth from His childhood, and likewise He was accustomed to attend the synagogues in every town where He preached, keeping the Jewish order and seizing these opportunities to preach. Synagogues were spread throughout Judea wherever ten families gathered, and readings from the Holy Scriptures and preaching were offered in them. Christ entered as was His custom to interpret the prophecies that referred to Him, for He did not come to destroy but to fulfill.

4.13.0.en: It was the custom in the synagogue that after the reading from the books of Moses, there would be a reading from the prophets, so He chose from the book of Isaiah these verses (Isa 61:1-2), which are like the speech from the throne announcing the beginning of the ministry of the awaited Messiah.

4.14.0.en: Isaiah spoke in the spirit of prophecy about the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the Messiah, who begins His ministry by preaching to the poor, whom the devil has humiliated and kept far from God; and everyone whose heart is broken because of his inability to fulfill the commandments, and likewise everyone whom the devil has bound with sin and who longs for the freedom of the glory of the children of God. And He opens the eyes of those whose eyes have been darkened by evil, and gives all the crushed and weak new life in Him.

4.15.0.en: The acceptable year of the Lord is the year of jubilee, which comes every fifty years (Lev 25:10), in which the land rests and is not sown, and slaves are set free. It refers to the time in which Christ preaches and redeems mankind to receive eternal life.

4.15.1.en: The beginning of Christ's preaching in Nazareth coincided with the year of jubilee among the Jews.

4.15.2.en: V. 20 He closed: the Holy Scriptures were written on skin parchments and rolled around a stick, so they were in the form of a cylinder; so after the reading he rolled it around the stick, that is, closed it.

4.15.3.en: The minister: the person responsible for keeping the Holy Scriptures in the synagogue.

4.15.4.en: He sat down: the custom in the synagogues of old was to stand when reading the Scriptures and then to sit for preaching, and the eyes of the people were fastened on Him, as He read the words with authority and power.

4.16.0.en: The Lord Christ interpreted the words of Isaiah about the Messiah, declaring their fulfillment now in Him, and thus He announced to them the beginning of the New Testament and the salvation that they had awaited.

4.16.1.en: Christ came for the sake of the weak to give them strength and freedom. So do not be disturbed by your weakness, and be confident that Christ loves you and supports you and has come for your sake.

4.17.0.en: Despite the amazement of the people of Nazareth at Christ's powerful words, they despised Him because He was the son of Joseph, the village carpenter. Because of their pride they looked at His social origin and did not benefit from His teachings.

4.17.1.en: Do you despise others, being haughty about your lineage or your abilities, and do not accept the word of God from their mouths or learn from their virtues?

4.17.2.en: V. 23 Done in Capernaum: it is understood that He visited Capernaum before Nazareth, and performed many miracles in it that St. Luke did not mention.

4.17.3.en: The divinity of Christ appeared in His exposing their thoughts that blamed Him, because He had performed many miracles in Capernaum, but when He came to Nazareth He performed only a few miracles, for they felt, selfishly, that they were more entitled than any other town to His miracles, and they considered this a weakness in Him and an inability to perform miracles among them.

4.18.0.en: Christ declared the reason for His not performing miracles among them, which was the weakness of their faith because of their pride and their not esteeming the power of their townsman, as happened with the prophets in the Old Testament, for their knowing the origin of the prophets in their childhood and youth made them despise and disbelieve their prophecies and teachings, so this became a common proverb among the Jews.

4.18.1.en: Do not be distressed if those close to you reject your word, but humble yourself and continue in your love, your prayers and your invitation to them to draw near to the Church.

4.19.0.en: Christ showed His acceptance of the Gentiles as well as the Jews, confirming that with events from the Old Testament.

4.19.1.en: In the days of Elijah, when famine spread, he performed the miracle with a Gentile widow from the city of Sarepta of Sidon, a city on the coast of the Mediterranean next to the city of Sidon, and he stayed with her and not with any Jewish widow, and blessed her house, preferring her over all the widows of the Jews, because of the readiness of her heart for faith (1 Kgs 17).

4.19.2.en: Likewise Elisha healed Naaman the Gentile, who was one of the enemies of the Jews, although there were many Jewish lepers whom he did not heal.

4.19.3.en: By this Christ confirmed His concern to perform miracles in Capernaum among the Gentiles because of their readiness for faith, whereas in His own town Nazareth He did not, because of their unbelief.

4.19.4.en: Examine yourself, lest the weakness of your faith and your not seeking God be the cause of hindering His work with you. And open your heart with love to all people and pray for them because they are children of God. And do not be vexed at God's helping them more than you, but let this drive you to draw near to Him with humility and supplication.

4.20.0.en: Christ exposed the thoughts of the people of Nazareth, and revealed their sins and declared the superiority of the Gentiles over them, and consequently that they deserved salvation like them, and even performed more miracles among them, so they were very angry instead of repenting, because of their pride; and in the hardness of their hearts they led Him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, to cast Him down headlong and kill Him.

4.20.1.en: Know that "the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God" (Jas 1:20). So do not make a decision in your anger, for it is wrong however right it may seem in your sight, and accept the counsel and rebuke of others, for it may be a message from God that you may repent.

4.21.0.en: Christ did not resist them, but with all confidence left them and went His way while they were occupied with one another in their anger, and thus He escaped from evil.

4.21.1.en: Wisdom requires you to flee from useless arguments, which may develop into anger and many insults. So seek useful speech and beneficial works for the salvation of your soul and others'.

4.22.s.en: (7) Casting out a demon in Capernaum

4.22.0.en: Jesus returned to Capernaum, which was a large city and a center for many Roman commanders, so idolatry spread in it, and corruption likewise.

4.22.1.en: The city of Capernaum is low, below sea level, while Nazareth is high on a mountain, therefore it says "came down."

4.22.2.en: Nazareth represents the pride that refuses to submit to God, while humble Capernaum accepts His word, therefore He performed many miracles in it. The meaning of the name Capernaum is the city of comfort and rest.

4.22.3.en: The sabbath days: the Jews used to gather on the Sabbath day in the synagogue to hear the readings and preaching, and Christ seized these opportunities to teach them, and when His fame spread they followed Him everywhere, so He taught them every day.

4.23.0.en: The teachings of Christ, and likewise His miracles, were distinguished in that He performs them with authority, and not like the prophets who ask God's power to accomplish their miracles; therefore the crowds were astonished at hearing Him and seeing His miracles in Capernaum.

4.24.0.en: Present in the synagogue was a man into whom a demon had entered, who could not bear the power of the teaching and was afraid of being in the presence of God, who has authority to judge the whole world, so he cried out in terror in the midst of the synagogue, declaring his weakness and fear, and bore witness to the divinity of Christ.

4.25.0.en: Christ refused to hear a testimony to Himself from Satan, and with authority commanded him to come out of the man, so he fell to the ground convulsing like epileptics, and the unclean spirit came out of him, and he regained his calm after the evil and tension had gone out of him. And the devil was not able to harm any member of him because of his fear of Christ. Do not accept the praise and flattery of the wicked, for it is false, and refuse dialogue with them, so that you keep your purity.

4.26.0.en: Those present marveled at Christ's authority over the demons, for none can do this but God, so how does this authority appear in a man living in their midst? ... But this was a motive, gradually, to their faith in the divinity of Christ.

4.27.0.en: The news of Christ's teachings, authority and divinity spread in all the regions around Capernaum, because, as we mentioned, it was a large city surrounded by many smaller cities.

4.27.1.en: Live uprightly with God, and be faithful in your service, confident that God's light and His work in you will affect many without your feeling it, and draw them to Christ.

4.28.s.en: (8) The healing of Simon's wife's mother

4.28.0.en: The custom was to go to the synagogue on the Sabbath fasting, so Peter invited Christ and the disciples to eat the main meal in his house. Because of this love, Christ also gave him love, for his wife's mother had been seized with a great fever and was suffering, so the people of the house asked Him to heal her.

4.28.1.en: Show love, and you will find a greater love from God.

4.29.0.en: Simon's wife's mother was lying on a bed on the ground, so Jesus stood on the ground beside her, and so was higher than she, that is, above her, and commanded the disease to leave her, as He had commanded Satan in the synagogue with authority to come out of the man, and the fever left her at once, and she regained all her strength so that she was able to rise and minister to Christ and the guests who were in the house.

4.29.1.en: Simon's wife's mother signifies the human soul weakened by sin and having lost its ability for spiritual work; but if Christ comes to it and responds to the intercession of others for it, it regains its spiritual strength and even serves them. The gift of Christ and His grace are complete, more than we ask or think.

4.30.0.en: When the sun of the Sabbath day set, it became permitted for the Jews to travel, as the day of rest had ended. So they hastened from Capernaum and the surrounding regions to the house of Simon Peter, carrying and leading their sick with their various diseases. Christ laid His hands on them, and a power went out from Him that gave them healing. Such is Christ's love for everyone in need.

4.31.0.en: In addition to the sick, they brought to Him many into whom demons had entered and humiliated them, and He cast them out of them, and as they came out they cried out in shame and fear, declaring that He was the Christ, but He forbade them to continue speaking thus because:

4.31.1.en: (1) He does not need the testimony of demons.

4.31.2.en: (2) It was not the right time to reveal Himself, lest this provoke the leaders and they crucify Him before He accomplished His ministry on earth.

4.31.3.en: (3) Because He does not seek glory from men, and by this He teaches us to flee from praise.

4.32.0.en: Christ spent the night in Capernaum. And early in the morning, without the crowds' knowing, He went out to a desert place in the wilderness to pray, to teach us the importance of retreat and prayer, so that we are satisfied with God's love and do not get lost amid worldly occupations, even if it is the service of God.

4.32.1.en: When the crowds looked for Him and did not find Him, they searched until they reached Him and asked Him insistently to stay with them out of their love for Him and admiration of Him, because He had healed their diseases, and they had heard from Him very great teachings.

4.33.0.en: Despite Christ's appreciation of their love and their holding on to Him, He declared to them the necessity of preaching in the other towns, for this was His mission for which He became incarnate, to save the whole world. He made clear that He was sent from God, to confirm that He is the awaited Messiah and not a new god independent of the old, well-known God. It is good that you care for all those around you and not only the people of your household, and call them all to the love of God and His holy Mysteries.

4.34.0.en: And Christ actually began to travel about the land of Galilee, the northern part of the land of the Jews, making use of the Jews' custom of welcoming itinerant preachers, to preach in the synagogues and proclaim salvation. Miracles of healing the sick and a catch of fish
